entries.title: Song of Solomon 3:1
segments: I sought him, but I found him not; the first five verses of this chapter describe the bride's longing desire after her beloved in his absence, and her unsuccessful search for him.

entries.title: Song of Solomon 3:4
segments:
Her that conceived me; spiritually interpreted, the bride's mother is not essentially different from the bride herself.  The one is the church viewed spiritually, in her power to produce and perpetuate a holy seed, and the other, the church viewed as that seed. 
 
Christ will be found of all who earnestly seek him in the ways of his appointment.

entries.title: Song of Solomon 3:5
segments: Till he please; see note to

entries.title: Song of Solomon 3:6
segments:
Who is this; a new picture.  The bride comes out of the wilderness to meet the heavenly Bridegroom, gloriously arrayed in wedding attire and fragrant with perfumes. 
 
  The wilderness; into which she has been banished.  This is a symbol of persecution and distress,
; the same as the winter season,

. 
 
  Like pillars of smoke; surrounded with clouds of fragrant incense. Her graces are a sweet savor to God. 
 
The church never appears so glorious as in her return to God by hearty repentance and faith, after the night of affliction and chastisement.

entries.title: Song of Solomon 3:8
segments:
Because of fear in the night; to guard against fear in the night. 
 
The church is safe in communion with her omnipotent Redeemer.

entries.title: Song of Solomon 3:9
segments: A chariot; this is for his bride and her companions, the daughters of Jerusalem.  Its precious materials represent the dignity and excellence of those who ride in it.

entries.title: Song of Solomon 3:10
segments: For the daughters of Jerusalem; more literally, "from the daughters of Jerusalem."  The midst of it is paved with their love for the King.

entries.title: Song of Solomon 3:11
segments: His mother crowned him; the church is the mother of the heavenly Solomon, the greatest of all her sons, and also his bride.  Compare
.  In the same way the church, viewed in one aspect, is the bride's mother; in another, the bride herself.  See note on

.  The Bridegroom and bride are also brother and sister. This blending of figures in allegory is both natural and beautiful. 
 
In his espousals to the church, Christ appears in heavenly glory, the object of unbounded love and admiration to all who belong to the household of faith.
